mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 1.15% signals an easing monetary cycle, reducing discount rates on equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during the easing period, or FEDFUNDS does not decline below 1.15% over the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the federal funds rate below 1.15% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over 20 trading days as investors anticipate further easing and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positively correlated with the rate decline (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not stay below 1.15% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (RSAFS) above their 5-year moving averages signals robust demand-side expansion, boosting corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both exceed their 5-year moving averages
failure_condition: 60-day returns fail to outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.05) despite the combined demand indicators exceeding thresholds, or the proxies do not move in tandem as expected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime marked by elevated GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (RSAFS), investors anticipate overvaluation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as profit-taking occurs.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite sustained high GDP and industrial production growth (p > 0.05), or the regime does not persist for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a strengthening labor market, prompting short-term positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as investors anticipate sustained economic growth.
failure_condition: 5-day returns fail to show significant positive correlation with the unemployment rate drop (p > 0.05), or UNRATE does not stay below 4.0% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing demand (HOUST) alongside falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a dual positive signal, driving S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days as investors anticipate both demand growth and lower borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and FEDFUNDS both rise above their 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to correlate positively with the combined HOUST-FEDFUNDS trend (p > 0.05), or the proxies do not move in tandem as expected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 105 in the index signals excess supply, leading to S&P 500 negative forward returns over 60 days as investors anticipate price adjustments and reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain positive despite INDPRO staying above 105 (p > 0.05), or the supply-side overproduction does not materialize as projected.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, simultaneous improvement in GDP growth (GDPC1) and federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals a turning point, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days as investors reassess growth prospects.
failure_condition: 5-day returns fail to rise significantly (p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 and FEDFUNDS improving, or the proxies do not move in tandem during the regime.
